headline: Omics machine learning benchmarks test generalization across populations and modalities
label: Benchmarking Omics Machine Learning Models
summary: Recent benchmarks shift omics model evaluation toward subgroup disparities, cross-modality transfer, and large-scale pipeline comparisons.
synthesis: The common thread is evaluation of omics machine learning models beyond the conditions under which they were developed. EHI provides an open benchmark of 1,475 multi-population deep learning tasks for omics-based cancer prognosis and quantifies performance disparities across populations, and a companion preprint reports that instruction-tuned tabular foundation models with in-context learning reduce ancestry-group gaps in genomic risk prediction. HADACA3 applies a comparative stance at larger scale, testing over 250,000 pipelines on nine DNA methylation and RNA datasets and finding that multi-omics integration does not beat DNAm alone for deconvolution. scTranslation benchmarks single-cell multi-omics modality translation. Most other published work consists of method papers, including PEARL, GEDI 2.0 with 40-64% lower peak memory, and THC-Net at 93.1% mean AUROC. What is distinct here is that subgroup disparity and negative multi-omics results are treated as primary outcomes rather than secondary observations.
